messages.content: You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My wifi shows connected but there is no internet

The adapter had no DNS server assigned and a stale DHCP lease. Flushing the DNS cache, restarting the Wi-Fi adapter, and renewing the IP lease restored connectivity (ping to 8.8.8.8 now succeeds).
Commands used:
- Test-NetConnection 8.8.8.8 -InformationLevel Quiet
- Get-DnsClientServerAddress -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object InterfaceAlias, ServerAddresses
- Clear-DnsClientCache
- Restart-NetAdapter -Name 'Wi-Fi'
- ipconfig /renew
- Test-NetConnection 8.8.8.8 -InformationLevel Quiet
Recommendation: If this recurs after sleep, update the Wi-Fi driver from the vendor site.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Websites won't load but ping to IP addresses works - looks like DNS is broken

Name resolution was failing because the configured DNS server was unreachable. Setting Cloudflare/Google DNS (1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8) and flushing the cache restored domain resolution.
Commands used:
- Resolve-DnsName microsoft.com -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- Set-DnsClientServerAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Wi-Fi' -ServerAddresses ('1.1.1.1','8.8.8.8')
- Clear-DnsClientCache
- Resolve-DnsName microsoft.com | Select-Object -First 1 Name, IPAddress
Recommendation: Keep DNS set to automatic unless your network requires a specific resolver.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My bluetooth headphones will not pair with the laptop

The Bluetooth Support Service (bthserv) was stopped, so the pairing UI could not discover devices. Setting it to Automatic and starting it brought the stack online and the headphones paired.
Commands used:
- Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Name, Status, StartType
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Set-Service bthserv -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service bthserv
- Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: Put the headphones in pairing mode (hold the power button until the LED blinks) before adding them in Settings.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The bluetooth toggle disappeared from Windows settings completely

The Bluetooth radio device was in an Error/Disabled state, which removes the toggle from Settings. Re-enabling the PnP device restored the radio and the toggle reappeared.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status, InstanceId
- Enable-PnpDevice -InstanceId 'USB\VID_8087&PID_0026\5&...' -Confirm:$false
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: If the toggle vanishes again after updates, reinstall the Bluetooth driver.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My PC is very slow and something is eating all the memory
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Task Manager shows disk at 100 percent constantly

Sustained 100% disk time on an HDD was driven by the SysMain (Superfetch) prefetch service. Disabling SysMain dropped disk activity to normal idle levels.
Commands used:
- Get-Service SysMain, WSearch | Select-Object Name, Status
- Get-Counter '\PhysicalDisk(_Total)\% Disk Time' -SampleInterval 1 -MaxSamples 3 | ForEach-Object { $_.CounterSamples.CookedValue }
- Stop-Service SysMain; Set-Service SysMain -StartupType Disabled
Recommendation: SysMain helps on SSDs but can thrash HDDs; leave it disabled on this machine, or upgrade to an SSD.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
I get access denied when trying to delete a leftover program folder

The leftover folder was owned by TrustedInstaller, causing Access Denied. Taking ownership, granting full control, and then removing it cleared the folder.
Commands used:
- Test-Path 'C:\Program Files\OldApp'
- takeown /f 'C:\Program Files\OldApp' /r /d y
- icacls 'C:\Program Files\OldApp' /grant *S-1-1-0:F /t
- Remove-Item 'C:\Program Files\OldApp' -Recurse -Force
Recommendation: Prefer the app's official uninstaller first; only force-delete leftovers when the uninstaller is gone.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Defender real-time protection turned off and won't stay on

No third-party antivirus was installed, so Defender was the active AV but real-time monitoring had been disabled. Re-enabling real-time monitoring restored protection.
Commands used:
- Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object RealTimeProtectionEnabled, AntivirusEnabled, AMServiceEnabled
- Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/SecurityCenter2 -ClassName AntiVirusProduct | Select-Object displayName
- Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring $false
- Get-MpComputerStatus | Select-Object RealTimeProtectionEnabled
Recommendation: If it disables itself again, run a full scan and check Task Scheduler / startup items for tampering.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Update is stuck downloading at 0 percent for hours

The BITS service was stopped and the SoftwareDistribution cache was corrupt, stalling the download. Stopping the update services, clearing the cache, and restarting them let the update download and install normally.
Commands used:
- Get-Service wuauserv, bits | Select-Object Name, Status
- Stop-Service wuauserv, bits -Force
- Rename-Item 'C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution' 'SoftwareDistribution.old' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- Start-Service wuauserv, bits
Recommendation: Re-run Windows Update; you can delete SoftwareDistribution.old once updates complete successfully.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Ethernet cable plugged in but no network connection

The adapter was up but had a self-assigned APIPA address (169.254.x), meaning DHCP had failed. Releasing and renewing the lease pulled a valid IP and restored the connection.
Commands used:
- Get-NetAdapter -Name 'Ethernet' | Select-Object Status, LinkSpeed
- Get-NetIPAddress -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv4 | Select-Object IPAddress
- ipconfig /release Ethernet; ipconfig /renew Ethernet
Recommendation: If APIPA returns, check the router's DHCP pool or cabling.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Wi-Fi is really slow even though signal is full

The laptop was connected on the crowded 2.4 GHz band at 802.11n (72 Mbps cap), not the faster 5 GHz band. Signal was fine; the band was the bottleneck.
Commands used:
- netsh wlan show interfaces
- Get-NetAdapter -Name 'Wi-Fi' | Select-Object LinkSpeed
Recommendation: Connect to the router's 5 GHz SSID for higher throughput, or move closer to the AP.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My VPN client fails to connect every time

The Remote Access Connection Manager (RasMan) service, required for VPN dial-up, was stopped. Setting it to Automatic and starting it let the VPN connect.
Commands used:
- Get-Service *vpn*, RasMan | Select-Object Name, Status
- Set-Service RasMan -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service RasMan
- Get-Service RasMan | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: Keep RasMan on Automatic so the VPN works after every reboot.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
One particular website won't open but everything else works

A leftover hosts-file entry pointed example.com to 127.0.0.1, so the browser hit the local machine instead of the real server. DNS itself resolves correctly.
Commands used:
- Select-String -Path "$env:SystemRoot\System32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Pattern 'example.com'
- Resolve-DnsName example.com | Select-Object -First 1 IPAddress
Recommendation: Remove the stale line from C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts (edit as Administrator).
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Network shows limited connectivity with a yellow warning triangle

Even the gateway was unreachable, pointing to a corrupt network stack. Resetting the Winsock catalog and the TCP/IP stack cleared the limited-connectivity state.
Commands used:
- Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 192.168.1.1 -InformationLevel Quiet
- netsh winsock reset
- netsh int ip reset
Recommendation: Reboot to finish applying the Winsock/TCP-IP reset.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Wi-Fi keeps disconnecting randomly every few minutes

Windows was powering down the Wi-Fi adapter to save energy, dropping the connection. Disabling the adapter's power-management setting stopped the random disconnects.
Commands used:
- Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name 'Wi-Fi' | Select-Object AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice
- Disable-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name 'Wi-Fi'
Recommendation: On laptops, keep this disabled while on AC power for stable Wi-Fi.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
No internet after uninstalling a program, proxy seems stuck

An uninstalled app left a system proxy pointing at a dead local port (127.0.0.1:8888), so all traffic was black-holed. Resetting the WinHTTP proxy to direct restored internet access.
Commands used:
- netsh winhttp show proxy
- netsh winhttp reset proxy
Recommendation: Also check Settings > Network > Proxy and turn off any manual proxy.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My bluetooth mouse is laggy and skips

The mouse device itself is healthy. On this laptop the Bluetooth radio shares the 2.4 GHz band with Wi-Fi power management, causing lag under load. Reducing radio power-saving smooths it out.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Where-Object FriendlyName -like '*mouse*' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Get-NetAdapterPowerManagement -Name 'Wi-Fi' | Select-Object AllowComputerToTurnOffDevice
Recommendation: Replace the mouse battery and keep it within 1-2 m of the laptop; interference from USB 3 hubs also causes skipping.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Bluetooth headset audio stutters when I also use the mic

When the mic is active, Windows switches the headset to the low-quality Hands-Free (HFP) profile, which causes the stutter and drop in audio quality. This is a Bluetooth profile limitation, not a fault.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice | Where-Object FriendlyName -like '*Hands-Free*' | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Recommendation: For music use the 'Stereo (A2DP)' playback device; only switch to the Hands-Free device for calls.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Bluetooth is completely missing from Device Manager

No Bluetooth radio was listed and the support service was disabled. Re-enabling and starting bthserv brought the stack back; the radio reappeared after a rescan.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Bluetooth | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
- Get-Service bthserv | Select-Object Status, StartType
- Set-Service bthserv -StartupType Manual; Start-Service bthserv
Recommendation: If the radio still doesn't appear, use 'Scan for hardware changes' in Device Manager or reinstall the Bluetooth driver.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Bluetooth file transfer to my phone keeps failing

The AVCTP transport service used for Bluetooth transfers was stopped. Starting it allowed the OBEX file push to complete.
Commands used:
- Get-Service BthAvctpSvc | Select-Object Name, Status
- Start-Service BthAvctpSvc
Recommendation: Accept the incoming file prompt on the phone promptly; the pairing can time out.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in bluetooth problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Bluetooth speaker pairs but there is no sound from it

The JBL speaker paired and appears as a healthy audio endpoint, but the default playback device was still the internal Realtek speakers, so all sound went there.
Commands used:
- Get-PnpDevice -Class AudioEndpoint | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Recommendation: Set the JBL device as Default in Settings > Sound (or click the volume icon and pick it).
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
One process is using 100 percent CPU and the fan is loud

A background 'WamiHost' process was pinned at very high CPU accumulation, driving the fan. Chrome was a distant second. The runaway process is the cause of the heat/noise.
Commands used:
- Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 3 Name, CPU, Id
Recommendation: If WamiHost is not a recognized app, end it and scan for unwanted software; if it is a known app, update or reinstall it.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My laptop takes forever to become usable after login

Several heavy apps (Steam, OneDrive, Spotify) launch at login and compete for disk and CPU, slowing the desktop right after sign-in.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | Select-Object Name, Command
Recommendation: Open Task Manager > Startup and disable apps you don't need immediately at boot.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My C drive is almost full and I don't know what's using it
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU stays high even when I'm not doing anything

Windows Defender's real-time engine (MsMpEng) was doing a background scan, which is normal but pushes idle CPU up temporarily. No malicious process was found.
Commands used:
- Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select-Object -First 5 Name, CPU
Recommendation: Let the scan finish; if MsMpEng is always high, add large dev folders to Defender exclusions.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
PC freezes for a few seconds after waking from sleep

The brief post-wake freeze is the system re-initializing devices from S3 sleep on the Balanced plan; nothing is faulty. Disk and drivers reload for a few seconds.
Commands used:
- powercfg /getactivescheme
- powercfg /a
Recommendation: Update chipset/storage drivers; on desktops with SSDs the High Performance plan reduces the wake stutter.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows boots very slowly on my HDD

Boot is slow because the OS is on a mechanical HDD with 14 startup programs. The disk is healthy; the media type is the main limiter for boot speed.
Commands used:
- Get-PhysicalDisk | Select-Object MediaType, HealthStatus, Size
- Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
Recommendation: Trim startup apps now; the biggest win is cloning Windows onto an SSD.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in performance problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
An app slowly eats all my RAM until I restart it

Teams had grown to ~2.4 GB working set, a known memory-leak pattern for long-running Electron apps. The rest of the system is fine.
Commands used:
- Get-Process Teams -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, @{N='MB';E={[int]($_.WorkingSet64/1MB)}}
Recommendation: Fully quit and reopen Teams periodically, and update it to the latest version where the leak is reduced.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
A document is corrupted and Word won't open it

The document exists but is 0 bytes, so its contents were lost (often from an interrupted save or a bad sync). There is no data left inside the file itself to open.
Commands used:
- Test-Path 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\report.docx'
- Get-Item 'C:\Users\Public\Documents\report.docx' | Select-Object Length
Recommendation: Restore an earlier copy from File History, OneDrive version history, or the Recycle Bin.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The Recycle Bin is corrupted and throws an error

The per-drive $Recycle.Bin metadata folder was corrupt, causing the error. Removing it forces Windows to recreate a clean Recycle Bin on the next delete.
Commands used:
- Test-Path 'C:\$Recycle.Bin'
- Remove-Item 'C:\$Recycle.Bin' -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Recommendation: It regenerates automatically; just delete any file to rebuild it.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
I can't rename a file because it says it's open in another program

Excel (PID 7788) still had budget.xlsx open, which locks the file and blocks the rename.
Commands used:
- Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.Modules.FileName -like '*budget.xlsx*' } | Select-Object Name, Id
Recommendation: Save and close the file in Excel, then rename; if Excel is hung, end its task first.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My folder looks empty but I know there are files in it

The folder actually holds 27 items, but they carry the Hidden attribute, so Explorer wasn't showing them with default settings.
Commands used:
- Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\data' -Force | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
- Get-ChildItem 'C:\Users\Public\data' -Force -Hidden | Select-Object -First 2 Name
Recommendation: Turn on 'Hidden items' in Explorer's View tab, or clear the hidden attribute with attrib -h.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
I get a path too long error copying some files

Windows long-path support was disabled (LongPathsEnabled=0), so paths over 260 characters failed. Enabling it allows long paths for compliant apps.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem' -Name LongPathsEnabled | Select-Object LongPathsEnabled
- Set-ItemProperty 'HKLM:\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\FileSystem' -Name LongPathsEnabled -Value 1
Recommendation: Reboot for it to take full effect; some older apps still cap at 260 chars regardless.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in file problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Access denied when opening a folder on a mapped network drive

The Z: mapping to \\server\finance is connected, but the logged-in user (anita) lacks NTFS/share permissions on that folder, producing Access Denied.
Commands used:
- whoami
- Get-SmbMapping | Select-Object LocalPath, RemotePath, Status
Recommendation: Ask the file-server admin to grant your account access to the finance share; this can't be fixed from the client side.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Firewall is blocking my app from connecting

The firewall was on for all profiles and had no rule for the app, so inbound connections were blocked. Adding an Allow rule scoped to the app's executable unblocked it without disabling the firewall.
Commands used:
- Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name, Enabled
- New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Allow MyApp' -Direction Inbound -Program 'C:\Apps\MyApp\myapp.exe' -Action Allow
Recommendation: Prefer per-app allow rules over turning the firewall off.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
I see a suspicious program launching at startup

A startup entry named 'updater' runs C:\Users\Public\svchost.exe — a legit system name in a very suspicious user-writable location. This is a classic malware masquerading pattern.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | Select-Object Name, Command, Location
Recommendation: Do not run it. Run a full Microsoft Defender offline scan and, if confirmed malicious, remove the HKCU Run entry and the file.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Run a quick malware scan, I think something is off

A Defender quick scan completed and reported no threat detections. The system is clean per the quick scan.
Commands used:
- Start-MpScan -ScanType QuickScan
- Get-MpThreatDetection | Select-Object -First 3 ThreatID, ActionSuccess
Recommendation: For peace of mind run a Full scan overnight; keep real-time protection on.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My Windows Firewall got turned off somehow

All three firewall profiles were disabled, leaving the machine exposed. Re-enabling the firewall on every profile restored protection.
Commands used:
- Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name, Enabled
- Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Private,Public -Enabled True
Recommendation: Check what disabled it (a game 'optimizer' or malware); keep the firewall on.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
There have been lots of failed login attempts, is someone trying to get in

Several 4625 (failed logon) events occurred within seconds of each other overnight, consistent with an automated password-guessing attempt against the account.
Commands used:
- Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4625} -MaxEvents 5 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object TimeCreated
Recommendation: Set a strong password, enable account lockout, and if this is remotely reachable, disable RDP from the internet or put it behind a VPN.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in security problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
SmartScreen keeps blocking a program I trust

SmartScreen/PUA protection is on and flags the app because it lacks a known reputation (common for small or new publishers), not necessarily because it's malicious.
Commands used:
- Get-MpPreference | Select-Object PUAProtection
Recommendation: If you're certain of the source, choose 'More info > Run anyway'. Only bypass SmartScreen for files you truly trust.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Search stopped working, typing in the box finds nothing

The Windows Search service had stopped, so the index wasn't answering queries. Starting it restored search results.
Commands used:
- Get-Service WSearch | Select-Object Status, StartType
- Start-Service WSearch
- Get-Service WSearch | Select-Object Status
Recommendation: If results stay stale, rebuild the index from Indexing Options.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My printer shows offline even though it is on

The spooler was running but in a stuck state, showing the printer offline. Restarting the Print Spooler cleared the stuck status and the printer returned to Normal.
Commands used:
- Get-Service Spooler | Select-Object Status
- Restart-Service Spooler -Force
- Get-Printer | Select-Object Name, PrinterStatus
Recommendation: If it goes offline again, clear stuck jobs and uncheck 'Use Printer Offline'.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My Start menu won't open when I click it

The Explorer shell that hosts the Start menu had gotten into a bad state. Restarting explorer.exe rebuilt the shell and the Start menu opened again.
Commands used:
- Get-Process explorer | Select-Object Id, StartTime
- Stop-Process -Name explorer -Force; Start-Process explorer
Recommendation: If it recurs after updates, run 'sfc /scannow' to check shell components.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
The clock shows the wrong time and won't sync

The Windows Time service (W32Time) was stopped, so the clock drifted and couldn't sync. Starting the service and forcing a resync corrected the time.
Commands used:
- Get-Service W32Time | Select-Object Status
- Start-Service W32Time; w32tm /resync
Recommendation: Ensure W32Time startup is Automatic (or 'Automatic (Delayed)') so it syncs at boot.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Microsoft Store apps won't open at all

The Client License Service (ClipSVC), which Store apps need to validate licenses, was stopped, so the apps failed to launch. Starting it let them open.
Commands used:
- Get-Service ClipSVC, wuauserv | Select-Object Name, Status
- Start-Service ClipSVC
Recommendation: If they still fail, run 'wsreset.exe' to clear the Store cache.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
My second monitor is not being detected

Only one monitor is active at the OS level, so the second display isn't being seen — usually a cable/input or driver handshake issue rather than a Windows fault.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorBasicDisplayParams | Measure-Object | Select-Object Count
- Get-PnpDevice -Class Monitor | Select-Object Status, FriendlyName
Recommendation: Press Win+P and choose Extend, reseat the HDMI/DP cable and select the right input, then update the GPU driver.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Windows Update keeps failing with an error code

Two services Windows Update depends on (BITS and Windows Installer) were stopped, causing the update to fail. Starting them lets the update engine work again.
Commands used:
- Get-Service wuauserv, cryptSvc, bits, msiserver | Select-Object Name, Status
- Start-Service bits, msiserver
Recommendation: Re-run Windows Update; if it still fails, clear SoftwareDistribution and retry.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in windows problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
An old app looks blurry on my high-resolution screen

On a high-DPI screen Windows scales the UI up, and the legacy app doesn't support DPI scaling, so Windows bitmap-stretches it and it looks blurry. This is an app limitation, not a display fault.
Commands used:
- Get-CimInstance -Namespace root/wmi -ClassName WmiMonitorBasicDisplayParams | Select-Object MaxHorizontalImageSize
Recommendation: Right-click the app's .exe > Properties > Compatibility > Change high DPI settings > 'Override' and pick 'System (Enhanced)'.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in audio problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Microphone is connected but no apps can hear my voice

Microphone privacy setting was set to Deny, blocking all desktop apps from accessing the audio input. Changing the registry capability key to Allow restored microphone input.
Commands used:
- Get-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\microphone' -Name Value
- Set-ItemProperty -Path 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\CapabilityAccessManager\ConsentStore\microphone' -Name Value -Value 'Allow'
Recommendation: Check Settings > Privacy & Security > Microphone if specific apps still fail.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in storage problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
USB flash drive plugged in but not showing in File Explorer

The USB flash drive partition had no mount point or drive letter assigned. Assigning drive letter E: mounted the volume and made it accessible in File Explorer.
Commands used:
- Get-Volume | Where-Object DriveLetter -eq $null
- Get-Volume -FileSystemLabel 'USB_DRIVE' | Get-Partition | Set-Partition -NewDriveLetter 'E'
Recommendation: Ensure USB drives are formatted as FAT32 or NTFS for auto-mounting.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
High latency and high ping spikes in online games over Wi-Fi

Periodic background Wi-Fi network scanning by WLAN AutoConfig caused ping spikes. Temporarily disabling autoconfig stopped background scans during active connections.
Commands used:
- netsh wlan show autoconfig
- netsh wlan set autoconfig enabled=no interface='Wi-Fi'
Recommendation: Remember to re-enable autoconfig when switching Wi-Fi networks.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in system problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Task Scheduler error prevents automated backup task from running

The Task Scheduler service (Schedule) was unexpectedly stopped. Starting the service enabled scheduled tasks to run normally.
Commands used:
- Get-Service Schedule | Select-Object Status, StartType
- Start-Service Schedule
Recommendation: Ensure Task Scheduler startup type remains on Automatic.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in network problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
Cannot connect to local development server on port 8080

The local application was bound and listening on port 8080, but incoming local network traffic was blocked by Windows Firewall. Created an inbound firewall rule for TCP port 8080.
Commands used:
- Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8080 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
- New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName 'Dev Server 8080' -Direction Inbound -LocalPort 8080 -Protocol TCP -Action Allow
Recommendation: Remove this rule if you stop running the local server.
You are a Windows repair expert specializing in cpu problems. Diagnose with read-only commands first, then apply safe fixes.
CPU is pinned at 100% by 'Windows Modules Installer Worker' for hours

TiWorker.exe (Windows Modules Installer Worker) was actively processing a pending update payload in the background, which is CPU-intensive but expected -- it is not malware.
Commands used:
- Get-Process TiWorker -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object Name, CPU
